This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants also increase the risk of infection when used with live vaccines. 3. Adalimumab decreases the effectiveness of hepatitis A/B vaccines through pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants elevate the risk of infection when administered with live vaccines. 4. Adalimumab reduces the efficacy of the hepatitis A/typhoid vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Adalimumab diminishes the effectiveness of the hepatitis B vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. This combination is contraindicated. Immunosuppressants increase the risk of infection when co-administered with live vaccines. 6. Adalimumab reduces the efficacy of the human papillomavirus (HPV) nonavalent vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Immunosuppressive therapies, including radiation, antimetabolites, alkylating agents, cytotoxic drugs, and corticosteroids (at doses exceeding physiological levels), may impair immune responses to vaccines. 7. Adalimumab and hydroxychloroquine sulfate both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 8. Hydroxyurea and adalimumab may increase the risk of immunosuppression. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Adalimumab and idecabtagene vicleucel both amplify each other's immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Patients on concurrent immunosuppressants or with impaired immune systems should be monitored closely due to an increased risk of serious infections. 26. Adalimumab increases and maitake decreases immunosuppressive effects, leading to a risk of infection. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 27. Use caution and monitor closely. Individuals with altered immune competence may have reduced immune responses to the vaccine. 31. Adalimumab and mercaptopurine both enhance immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Methotrexate reduces the levels of adalimumab by decreasing renal clearance. This interaction is minor, and dosage adjustment is not required. Methotrexate reduced adalimumab clearance by 29% after a single dose and 44% after multiple doses. 33. When co-administering immunosuppressive therapies, consider the risk of additive immune system effects. When switching from therapies with immune effects, account for the duration and mechanism of action of these therapies when initiating ofatumumab SC. 37. Adalimumab and olaparib both increase pharmacodynamic synergism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration with other myelosuppressive anticancer agents, including DNA-damaging agents, may potentiate and prolong myelosuppressive toxicity. 38. Adalimumab reduces the efficacy of the inactivated poliovirus vaccine due to pharmacodynamic antagonism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. Avoid vaccination during chemotherapy or radiation therapy if possible, as antibody response might be suboptimal. Patients vaccinated within 14 days before starting or during immunosuppressive therapy should be revaccinated three months after therapy is discontinued if immune competence has been restored. 41. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of rozanolixizumab with medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor may lower systemic exposures and effectiveness of such medications. Monitor closely for reduced effectiveness of medications that bind to the human neonatal Fc receptor. If long-term use of such medications is essential, consider discontinuing rozanolixizumab and using alternative therapies. 46. Adalimumab and selinexor have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Patients treated with selinexor may experience neurological toxicities. Avoid taking selinexor with other medications that may cause dizziness or confusion. 47. Adalimumab diminishes the effectiveness of the recombinant zoster vaccine via pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. Immunosuppressive therapies may reduce the effectiveness of the recombinant zoster vaccine. 68. Approximately 1-1% of maternal serum levels of adalimumab are transferred to breast milk. There are no reports of adverse effects on breastfed infants or effects on milk production. The developmental and health benefits of breastfeeding should be considered alongside the mother’s clinical need for therapy and any potential adverse effects on the breastfed child from the drug or the underlying maternal condition. 69. Adalimumab is generally acceptable for use during pregnancy. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. 70. Adalimumab has a half-life of 10-20 days and a total body clearance of 12 mL/hr. 71. Administer the full amount of adalimumab in the syringe as directed. Use separate injection sites in the thigh or abdomen, rotate injection sites, and avoid injecting into areas where the skin is tender, bruised, or damaged.
